draft:
Greenwich House Theater is a small room, and BLUDLINE: A Hip-Hop Odyssey filled it in a way that made the size feel intentional. The stage was close, the audience was close, and the cast was right there. No distance to hide behind, and no need to hide. I was working within reach of what was happening, which meant every frame was either in it or not — and there's no middle ground in a space like that.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-50.jpg | Four performers at mic stands on a warmly lit stage, arms raised and mouths open mid-performance, with a woman seated to the left and set dressing including photos on the wall behind them]

BLUDLINE is Fermin Suero, Jr. and Pete White's retelling of the Odyssey through live hip-hop and R&B. Odysseus trying to get home, Telemachus trying to survive without him, a community that's gone sideways in the meantime. The cast was working constantly, trading verses and scenes, the energy rarely settling. That's a good condition to shoot in. There's always something about to happen.

The thing I kept coming back to across the night was the exchange between performers. The moments when two people were in the same frame and both of them were in it. Suero and White had that going right from the start. In the close frames, the call-and-response reads as a physical thing, not just a musical one: one performer gesturing toward the other, the other already responding before the line is done.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-118.jpg | Two performers at mic stands, one gesturing toward the other with a hand extended, both smiling mid-exchange, with a third performer seated and smiling in the background under stage lighting]

White on guitar was worth a dedicated frame or two on his own. When he was deep in a passage, the guitar came up and the body bent with it. Not performing for the room but working something out. I held on him through a stretch where he wasn't at the mic, just playing, and got a few frames where the concentration was right there on the surface.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-125.jpg | A guitarist in a blue striped jacket bent forward over a pale green electric guitar, eyes closed, deeply focused, with another musician partially visible behind him]

The wide shots from the full-ensemble moments were the ones that showed what Matchbook Fest is actually doing with this. Mix and Match Productions presents Matchbook Sparks as a way to put new work in front of an audience while it's still being built, and that energy was palpable in the room. The cast knew the material, but there was also something live about it, a readiness that a long run can sometimes sand down. The wide frames have the whole cast at the stands, everyone in motion, the set behind them still clearly a workshop-stage setup rather than a finished production design. That context travels with the images.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-154.jpg | Five performers on a darkly lit stage in a wide shot, arms raised and gesturing expressively at mic stands, with chairs and set pieces behind them and a blue-lit wall of frames in the background]

The female performers in the cast, Ladibree, Safa, and the others, were working in a different register when they had the mic alone. The solo vocal moments pulled the energy down to something more focused, and the room followed. I was watching for the frames where a performer was mid-phrase and the body had caught up to the lyric. Not posed, just in it. That's what I was after.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-120.jpg | A woman in a striped top and wide-leg jeans stands at a mic stand, eyes closed, singing, with a seated performer partially visible to the right and a red-and-white patterned chair in the background]

The tighter frames are where the documentation earns its keep for a production like this. BLUDLINE's in development, a work-in-progress in a festival context. The photos from a night like this are what the creative team has when they're writing the next draft, putting together a pitch deck, or applying for the residency or commission that gets the show to the next stage. A wide shot of the full cast at the stands shows the scope. A close frame of Suero mid-verse, hands up, mouth open, beard and glasses and a gold durag, shows who this is and why it matters.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-96.jpg | A bearded performer in a white shirt and orange head covering, arms raised with hands spread open, mouth open mid-performance, with another performer at a mic stand slightly behind him]

The night ended with the full cast at the stands, everyone in, everyone pushing. I was close enough that I didn't have to choose between the group frame and the individual face. I could get both.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-55.jpg | A guitarist in a blue striped jacket sings into a mic with mouth open wide, eyes closed, holding a pale green guitar, with another performer partially visible to the left]

If you've got a new work in development, a staged reading, a workshop run, a festival slot, and you need images that can travel with the project past opening night, get in touch.
corrected:
BLUDLINE: A Hip-Hop Odyssey at Greenwich House Theater

BLUDLINE: A Hip-Hop Odyssey was part one of Matchbook Spark Vol. 2, presented by Mix and Match Productions at The Greenwich House Theater, paired with The One-Man Odyssey. Fermin Suero, Jr. and Pete White wrote it and perform in it, a retelling of the Odyssey through live hip-hop and R&B. Odysseus trying to get home, Telemachus trying to survive without him, a community that's gone sideways in the meantime.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-50.jpg | Four BLUDLINE performers at mic stands, arms raised mid-song, at Greenwich House Theater, with a seated cast member at left]

This was a concert performance, everyone at a mic stand, so I knew where the frames would be before it started. What changed through the night was who was turned toward whom.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-118.jpg | Two BLUDLINE performers at mic stands mid-exchange, one gesturing toward the other, a third seated behind, at Greenwich House Theater]

Suero and White perform alongside Phillip Johnson Richardson, Alaman, Ladibree, Safa, Alexander Manuel, and Taylor Fagins. Eight people at mic stands means the group frames fill up fast.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-154.jpg | Wide view of five BLUDLINE performers at mic stands under blue stage light at Greenwich House Theater, arms raised]

White was on guitar as well as vocals, sometimes both at once.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-125.jpg | Pete White bent over a pale green electric guitar in a blue striped jacket at Greenwich House Theater, another musician behind him]

I worked from the back of the house with room to move along the back wall and down house right.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-120.jpg | Safa singing at a mic stand in a striped top and wide-leg jeans at Greenwich House Theater, a seated performer to her right]

Fixed positions and a long lens meant the solo turns were the easiest to isolate.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-96.jpg | Fermin Suero, Jr. in a white shirt and orange head covering, arms raised and hands open mid-verse, at Greenwich House Theater]

BLUDLINE is still in development. The photos from a night like this are what the creative team has when they're writing the next draft, building a pitch deck, or applying for the residency or commission that moves the show forward.

[PHOTO: BLUDLINE- A Hip-Hop Odyssey (Greenwich House Theater) @dwphotony-55.jpg | Pete White sings into a mic while holding his pale green guitar at Greenwich House Theater, another performer partly visible at left]

If you've got new work in development, a staged reading, a workshop run, a festival slot, and you need images that travel with the project past opening night, get in touch.
